neighbours.label: verb or auxiliary at the point where an authority grants, awards or instructs (authority to grant, will be awarded, the students were asked)
fire: Under the charter, the board has the authority to grant licences to new schools.
Extra time will be given to candidates who provide a medical certificate.
At the end of the workshop, the trainees were asked to fill in a short questionnaire.
Only the dean has the power to grant an exemption from the final exam.
A certificate will be awarded to every participant who completes the course.
Before the quiz, the pupils were instructed to put away their notes.
No refunds will be issued after the first week of term.
The court may grant the tenant an extension of thirty days.
quiet: Under the old roof, the boards were damp and beginning to rot.
The afternoon will be warm, with a light breeze from the south.
At the end of the hike, the scouts were hungry and covered in mud.
Only the dean seemed surprised by the size of the crowd.
The harvest will be late this year because of the frost.
Before the storm, the pupils were playing football in the yard.
The river will be frozen by the first week of December.
The tenant painted the kitchen a pale shade of yellow.

notes: The + pole's output promotes ' assigned' / ' allocated' and its top examples are 'God-given' and 'was given'; this pole fires one step earlier, on the auxiliary or the granting verb.
